name: crime_rhe_beyond_2_22
description: Test 19 (spec answer C4). rhe(x) := int32(bits(f32(f32(x) + 12582912.0f)) - 0x4B400000) with a wrapping subtraction; exact round-half-even only for |x| <= 2^22. Beyond that the float32 sum loses bits and its exponent grows, so the bit difference no longer equals x: 4,194,304 -> 4,194,304; 4,194,305 -> sum 16,777,217 rounds to even 16,777,216 (2^24) -> 4,194,304; 4,194,307 -> 16,777,219 -> 16,777,220 = 0x4B800002 -> 4,194,306; 5,000,000 -> 17,582,912 = 0x4B8625A0 -> 4,597,152; 8,388,608 -> 20,971,520 = 0x4BA00000 -> 6,291,456; 100,000,000 -> 112,582,912 = 0x4CD6BC20 -> 26,655,776; -5,000,000 -> 7,582,912 = 0x4AE76980 (exponent 22, below 0x4B400000) -> -5,805,696 (wrapping). Small values keep round-half-even: 2.5 -> 2, 3.5 -> 4, -2.5 -> -2. Special inputs (x87 addition): +inf -> 0x7F800000 -> 876,609,536; -inf -> 0xFF800000 -> -1,270,874,112; a quiet NaN propagates (0x7FC00000 -> 880,803,840; 0xFFC00000 -> -1,266,679,808) and a signalling one is quieted (0x7F800001 -> 0x7FC00001 -> 880,803,841). Crimes to commit (6.4): a modded crimes curve constant -1 (0x8A0CBAAA = (0, -1), (1, -1)) with criminal base 200, no jail, no release and factor 1.0: trunc(-1) = -1, float(uint32 0xFFFFFFFF) = 4,294,967,295 -> f32 2^32, x 1.0, + 12,582,912 -> 4,307,550,208 = 0x4F806000 -> 71,327,744 (the earlier i32 saturation gave 2,147,483,647). A constant 50,000,000 -> 62,582,912 = 0x4C6EBC20 -> 19,840,032. All by hand, cross-checked with an independent numpy float32 model.
